subject: science
chapter_title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral

concepts.title: Nature as Our Science Laboratory
concepts.definition: Turmeric stains turn red with soap, tamarind cleans tarnished copper, lemon juice brightens dull brass: nature hides chemistry in every kitchen, making it our first science laboratory.
concepts.key_idea: The kitchen and garden are laboratories: everyday colour changes are chemical clues.

concepts.title: Acidic, Basic and Neutral Substances
concepts.definition: Substances fall into three families: acidic ones like lemon juice and vinegar, basic ones like soap and lime water, and neutral ones like pure water; litmus and turmeric papers reveal each family by colour.
concepts.key_idea: Three families sort the substance world: the indicator's colour names the family instantly.

concepts.title: Making and Using Indicators
concepts.definition: Indicators can be made at school: litmus solution and papers, turmeric paper and other natural dyes change colour in the presence of acids or bases and so announce a substance's family.
concepts.key_idea: An indicator is a chemical messenger: its colour change is a signal we can read.

concepts.title: Neutralisation in Daily Life
concepts.definition: When an acid and a base mix, they cancel each other into a neutral substance with salt and water, called neutralisation: antacid calms excess stomach acid, lime sweetens sour soil, and a bee sting's acid is soothed with a mild base.
concepts.key_idea: Neutralisation is chemistry's balancing act: the right opposite cancels the trouble.
